# orchestra_pipeline (Resource)

An Orchestra pipeline, with its definition in `data`.

Pipelines whose definition lives in a git repository are managed by Orchestra's git sync, not by Terraform.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An Orchestra-backed pipeline: Terraform owns the definition.
resource "orchestra_pipeline" "daily_sales" {
  alias     = "daily_sales"
  published = true

  data = {
    name = "Daily sales"

    # Task IDs and group IDs share one namespace, because the API merges
    # `tasks` and `task_groups` into a single object.
    tasks = {
      ingest = {
        integration     = "FIVETRAN"
        integration_job = "FIVETRAN_SYNC_ALL"

        # `parameters` is free-form in the API — its shape depends on
        # `integration_job` — so Terraform carries it as JSON.
        parameters = jsonencode({
          connector_id = "warehouse_orders"
        })
      }
    }

    task_groups = {
      transform = {
        depends_on = ["ingest"]
        name       = "Transform"

        tasks = {
          dbt_build = {
            integration     = "DBT_CORE"
            integration_job = "DBT_CORE_EXECUTE"
            connection      = "name_ABCD"

            parameters = jsonencode({
              commands        = "dbt build --select tag:daily"
              package_manager = "PIP"
              python_version  = "3.12"
            })

            configuration = {
              retries     = 2
              retry_delay = 60
              timeout     = 3600
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }

    schedule = [{
      name     = "nightly"
      cron     = "cron(0 2 * * ? *)"
      timezone = "Europe/London"
    }]

    # One run at a time; a run that starts while one is in progress waits.
    configuration = {
      concurrency = {
        max_active = "1"
        on_limit   = "QUEUE"
      }
    }

    alerts = [{
      name     = "notify_on_failure"
      statuses = ["FAILED"]

      destinations = [{
        integration = "SLACK"
        destination = "#data-alerts"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `alias` (String) Unique identifier. Letters, numbers and underscores only, max 255 characters. Changing it replaces the pipeline.
- `data` (Attributes) The pipeline definition: its tasks, schedule, sensors and alerts. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data))
- `paused` (Boolean) Whether the pipeline is paused. A paused pipeline's schedules, sensors, trigger events and API starts do not start new runs. Leave unset to leave it as it is, so a pause made in the Orchestra UI is not undone by the next apply.
- `published` (Boolean) Whether the pipeline is published and can be triggered.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the pipeline was created.
- `id` (String) The pipeline ID.
- `latest_version_number` (Number) Highest saved version number.
- `name` (String) The pipeline name, taken from `data.name` or from the YAML in the repository.
- `num_tasks` (Number) Number of tasks in the pipeline.
- `published_version_number` (Number) Version number currently published.
- `updated_at` (String) When the pipeline was last updated.
- `yaml_path` (String) Path to the pipeline YAML file, assigned by Orchestra.

<a id="nestedatt--data"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data`

Required:

- `name` (String) Unique identifier for this pipeline (max 100 chars). Used in UI and API.

Optional:

- `alerts` (Attributes List) Alerts to send when the pipeline run completes. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--alerts))
- `anomalies` (Attributes List) Pipeline duration anomaly monitors. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--anomalies))
- `configuration` (Attributes) Default retry and timeout settings inherited by all tasks. Task-level `configuration` overrides these. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--configuration))
- `inputs` (Attributes Map) Declared runtime inputs keyed by input name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--inputs))
- `meta` (String) Arbitrary metadata for external tooling, as a JSON object. The API accepts any shape here, so Terraform carries it as JSON — use `jsonencode({...})`.
- `schedule` (Attributes List) Cron schedules that trigger this pipeline. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--schedule))
- `sensors` (Attributes Map) Sensors keyed by sensor ID. A sensor triggers the pipeline once all of its checks pass. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--sensors))
- `task_groups` (Attributes Map) Task groups keyed by group ID. Groups are the primary way to build a DAG; dependencies between them define execution order. Group IDs must not collide with `tasks` keys — both are merged into the API's single `pipeline` object. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--task_groups))
- `tasks` (Attributes Map) Standalone top-level tasks keyed by task ID, for pipelines that do not need grouping. Task IDs must not collide with `task_groups` keys. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--tasks))
- `trigger_events` (Attributes List) Pipeline completion events that trigger this pipeline. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--trigger_events))
- `version` (String) Pipeline schema version. Currently only `v1` is supported.
- `webhook` (Attributes) Webhook configuration for manual and API triggers. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--webhook))

<a id="nestedatt--data--alerts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.alerts`

Required:

- `destinations` (Attributes List) Where to send the alert. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--alerts--destinations))
- `name` (String) Alert name.
- `statuses` (List of String) Run statuses that fire this alert.

Optional:

- `custom_message` (String) Custom alert message (max 200 chars).
- `max_live_alerts` (String) Maximum simultaneous live alerts. The API accepts an integer or a `${{ }}` template, so Terraform carries both as a string.

<a id="nestedatt--data--alerts--destinations"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.alerts.destinations`

Required:

- `integration` (String) Notification integration to send through.

Optional:

- `body` (String) Webhook request body, JSON-encoded. Only valid when `integration = "WEBHOOK"`. The API accepts an object or a string, so encode either — `jsonencode({...})` or `jsonencode("text")`.
- `connection_id` (String) Connection to authenticate the delivery with.
- `destination` (String) Where to deliver: an email address, Slack channel, or webhook URL, depending on `integration`.
- `priority` (Number) Datadog notification priority (1-5). Only valid when `integration = "DATADOG"`.



<a id="nestedatt--data--anomalies"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.anomalies`

Required:

- `type` (String) Which anomaly to monitor for.

Optional:

- `destinations` (Attributes List) Where to send the anomaly alert. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--anomalies--destinations))
- `min_baseline_seconds` (Number) Skip monitoring when the baseline is shorter than this (max 86400). Defaulted by Orchestra when not set.
- `percentage_above_baseline` (Number) Trigger when duration exceeds the baseline by this percentage (1-1000). Only valid for `*_above_baseline` types. Defaulted by Orchestra when not set.
- `percentage_below_baseline` (Number) Trigger when duration falls below the baseline by this percentage (1-99). Only valid for `*_below_baseline` types. Defaulted by Orchestra when not set.

<a id="nestedatt--data--anomalies--destinations"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.anomalies.destinations`

Required:

- `integration` (String) Notification integration to send through.

Optional:

- `body` (String) Webhook request body, JSON-encoded. Only valid when `integration = "WEBHOOK"`. The API accepts an object or a string, so encode either — `jsonencode({...})` or `jsonencode("text")`.
- `connection_id` (String) Connection to authenticate the delivery with.
- `destination` (String) Where to deliver: an email address, Slack channel, or webhook URL, depending on `integration`.
- `priority` (Number) Datadog notification priority (1-5). Only valid when `integration = "DATADOG"`.



<a id="nestedatt--data--configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.configuration`

Optional:

- `concurrency` (Attributes) Concurrency limits. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--configuration--concurrency))
- `retries` (Number) Number of times to retry on failure.
- `retry_delay` (Number) Seconds to wait between retries.
- `timeout` (Number) Timeout in seconds, from 0 to 259200 (72 hours).

<a id="nestedatt--data--configuration--concurrency"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.configuration.concurrency`

Optional:

- `max_active` (String) Maximum concurrent runs. The API accepts an integer or a `${{ }}` template, so Terraform carries both as a string (for example `"3"`).
- `on_limit` (String) What happens to a run that would exceed `max_active`: `SKIP` it, `QUEUE` it, or `QUEUE_LATEST` to keep only the newest waiting run. Also accepts a `${{ }}` template. Defaulted by Orchestra (to `SKIP`) when not set.



<a id="nestedatt--data--inputs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.inputs`

Required:

- `type` (String) Data type of the input.

Optional:

- `default` (String) Default value used when the input is not supplied at runtime. The API accepts any type here, so Terraform carries it JSON-encoded — `jsonencode("a string")`, `jsonencode(3)`, `jsonencode([1,2])`.
- `optional` (Boolean) If true, the input can be omitted even without a default value. Defaults to `false`.
- `options` (List of String) Fixed list of values this input is allowed to take. Only valid on inputs of `type = "string"`.


<a id="nestedatt--data--schedule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.schedule`

Required:

- `cron` (String) AWS EventBridge cron expression.

Optional:

- `branch` (String) Branch to run from, for git-backed pipelines.
- `environment` (String) Environment name or ID to run in.
- `exclude` (List of String) Dates (YYYY-MM-DD) to skip.
- `name` (String) Schedule name for display and reference.
- `run_inputs` (String) Input values to pass on each scheduled run, as a JSON object.
- `timezone` (String) IANA timezone for schedule evaluation.


<a id="nestedatt--data--sensors"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.sensors`

Required:

- `checks` (Attributes Map) Checks that must all pass before the pipeline is triggered, keyed by check ID. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--sensors--checks))
- `cron` (String) Cron expression defining when the sensor evaluation window opens.
- `name` (String) Sensor name for display and reference (max 100 chars).
- `timeout_mins` (Number) Maximum minutes to wait for all checks to pass (max 7200).
- `timezone` (String) IANA timezone for schedule evaluation.

Optional:

- `alerts` (Attributes List) Alerts to send for this sensor. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--sensors--alerts))
- `condition` (String) Expression using `${{ }}` syntax, evaluated after all checks pass and before triggering the pipeline.
- `environments` (List of String) Environments to run in when the sensor fires.
- `exclude` (List of String) Dates (YYYY-MM-DD) to skip sensor evaluation.
- `frequency_secs` (Number) How often checks are evaluated within the open window, in seconds (60-600).
- `run_inputs` (String) Input values to pass when the sensor triggers the pipeline, as a JSON object.

<a id="nestedatt--data--sensors--checks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.sensors.checks`

Required:

- `integration` (String) Integration platform for this check.
- `parameters` (String) Check parameters, as a JSON object. The shape depends on `sensor_type`, so the API declares it free-form — use `jsonencode({...})`.
- `sensor_type` (String) Type of sensor check to perform.

Optional:

- `connection` (String) Named connection to use for this check.
- `map_outputs` (Map of String) Maps check result fields to pipeline outputs.

<a id="nestedatt--data--task_groups"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.task_groups`

Required:

- `tasks` (Attributes Map) Task definitions within this group, keyed by task ID. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--task_groups--tasks))

Optional:

- `condition` (String) Expression using `${{ expression }}` syntax applied to every task in the group.
- `depends_on` (List of String) IDs of other top-level entries that must complete before this group runs.
- `matrix` (Attributes) Run the group multiple times with varying inputs. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--task_groups--matrix))
- `meta` (String) Arbitrary metadata for external tooling, as a JSON object.
- `name` (String) Human-readable name for the group (max 100 chars).
- `paused` (Boolean) When true, no task in this group runs.

<a id="nestedatt--data--task_groups--tasks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.task_groups.tasks`

Required:

- `integration` (String) The integration platform (SNOWFLAKE, DBT, AWS_ECS, etc.).
- `integration_job` (String) The operation to perform. Must be compatible with the integration.
- `parameters` (String) Integration-specific parameters, as a JSON object. The shape depends on `integration_job`, so the API declares it free-form and Terraform carries it as JSON — use `jsonencode({...})`.

Optional:

- `alerts` (Attributes List) Alerts to send when the task completes. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--task_groups--tasks--alerts))
- `anomalies` (Attributes List) Task and operation duration anomaly monitors. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--task_groups--tasks--anomalies))
- `condition` (String) Expression using `${{ expression }}` syntax that determines whether this task runs.
- `configuration` (Attributes) Task-specific retry and timeout settings. Overrides the pipeline-level `configuration`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--task_groups--tasks--configuration))
- `connection` (String) Named connection to use for this task's integration. Format: `name_XXXX`, or a `${{ }}` template.
- `depends_on` (List of String) IDs of tasks or groups that must complete before this task runs.
- `meta` (String) Arbitrary metadata for external tooling, as a JSON object.
- `name` (String) Human-readable name for display in the UI (max 100 chars).
- `operation_metadata` (Attributes Map) Per-integration operation metadata, keyed by metadata name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--task_groups--tasks--operation_metadata))
- `paused` (Boolean) When true, this task does not run. Downstream tasks execute as if it were not in the DAG.
- `tags` (List of String) Labels for filtering and organization (max 10 tags).
- `treat_failure_as_warning` (Boolean) If true, task failure results in WARNING status instead of FAILED.

<a id="nestedatt--data--task_groups--tasks--anomalies"></a>

- `max_parallel` (Number) Maximum concurrent matrix iterations.
- `sequential` (Boolean) If true, run iterations sequentially instead of in parallel.

<a id="nestedatt--data--trigger_events"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.trigger_events`

Required:

- `pipeline_id` (String) UUID of the pipeline whose completion triggers this one, or `*` for any pipeline.

Optional:

- `run_inputs` (String) Input values to pass to the triggered pipeline run, as a JSON object.
- `statuses` (List of String) Pipeline run statuses that fire the trigger.
- `type` (String) Event type. Currently only `pipeline` is supported.


<a id="nestedatt--data--webhook"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.webhook`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the webhook trigger is enabled.
- `operation_metadata` (Attributes Map) Per-integration operation metadata, keyed by metadata name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data--webhook--operation_metadata))
- `run_inputs` (String) Default input values for webhook-triggered runs, as a JSON object.

<a id="nestedatt--data--webhook--operation_metadata"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.webhook.operation_metadata`

Required:

- `integration` (String) Integration this metadata applies to.

Optional:

- `connection` (String) Named connection to use.
- `dbt_warehouse_identifier` (String) Warehouse identifier for dbt operation metadata.
- `s3_bucket_name` (String) S3 bucket to write operation metadata to.
- `s3_key_prefix` (String) Key prefix within the S3 bucket.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by alias.
terraform import orchestra_pipeline.daily_sales daily_sales

# Or by pipeline ID.
terraform import orchestra_pipeline.daily_sales 2b1f0f4e-6c5a-4f3e-9c6d-2a7b8c9d0e1f
```
